title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Competitor opening across the street
drivers.evidence: No prior data on competitor openings; effect shrunk toward 1.0. Recent price increase to $10.32 (4.5%) correlates with stable sales (96–104). Competitor entry likely reduces demand, but uncertainty is high.

drivers.name: Price increase (4.5% vs regular)
drivers.evidence: Same price point ($10.32) in two prior weeks (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) sold at 96–104 units (baseline: 96.6), indicating mild downside. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk to -3%.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 96.6. No events are scheduled, but a competitor opens across the street, which may reduce demand. Price is 4.5% above regular, which typically suppresses sales. The past promotion effect was x2.09 on average, but the following week saw x0.82, indicating post-promo pull-forward. The competitor opening is a new risk with no prior data; we shrink its effect toward 1.0. The price increase is moderate, and recent weeks at $10.32 show sales near baseline (96–104). The noise-adjusted effect of a competitor entry is uncertain, so we apply a small downside. The classical model suggests no lift, which aligns with no event. We adjust downward slightly for the competitor and price.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.32 (+4.5% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.6 | 5%-95%: 62.8 - 233.4 | 10%-90%: 67.4 - 191.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
